page.title: Best 4G LTE Security Camera With No WiFi (2026): Arenti GO3G vs eufy S330 vs Reolink
page.h1: Best 4G LTE security camera with no WiFi
page.desc: The cheapest honest 4G-only camera for a shed, lot or cabin, the best camera overall, and what every cellular camera costs you each month.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 4G LTE security camera with no WiFi on a budget is the Arenti GO3G ({buy:arenti-go3g-4g-lte-camera}): a 2K, 4G-only camera with a 10,400 mAh battery for $39.99 on 2026-11-06, with a SIM in the box and microSD recording up to 256 GB. The best camera overall is the eufy 4G LTE Cam S330, which costs $249.99 at eufy.com (2026-11-06) but gives you 4K video, a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi fallback and a standard EIOTCLUB SIM you top up as needed. Every cellular camera needs its own data plan once the trial ends, and guides that tested them put that at $10 to $40 a camera a month; the Arenti plan is bought inside the Arenti app and its price is not published outside it. Check that your carrier has 4G signal at the exact spot before you buy any of these.

Shoppers here split three ways. If you want to watch one remote spot for the least money and can live with a brand-locked plan, the Arenti GO3G wins on price by six to one. If you want the sharpest picture and a camera that keeps working when a nearby Wi-Fi network comes and goes, the eufy S330 wins. If you want 4K with no Wi-Fi at all and your own prepaid T-Mobile or AT&T data, the Reolink Go PT Ultra is the one to look at, though its price was not readable on reolink.com today.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Across the cellular cameras we read about, the same five problems keep coming up. The data plan is first: every one of the buying guides and listings we read says the camera stops streaming when the trial or plan runs out, and the brand-locked plans (Arenti, and many no-name cameras) cannot be swapped for a cheap carrier SIM. Coverage is second: a buyer with a remote hut needed a different carrier's SIM than the one in the box, and a Minnesota tester saw one to two bars of AT&T at his cabin. Winter battery is third: that same tester had to hand-charge his Reolink Go PT Ultra every few weeks below -10°F even with the solar panel, and Tom's Guide expects the eufy S330 to need topping up over winter. Data use is fourth: continuous HD streaming ate about 1 GB every two hours in security.org's test, so keep motion zones tight. For Arenti specifically, Trustpilot shows 61 reviews at 2.8 out of 5; slow support is the most common complaint (about 9 of the 21 visible reviews), followed by hardware that failed within a year and cloud plans that were hard to cancel. Arenti's app scores 4.5 out of 5 from about 1,900 ratings, with dropped connections and too many alerts the main gripes.

Which one by need

  • Cheapest watch on a remote spot: Arenti GO3G ({buy:arenti-go3g-4g-lte-camera}). 2K, pan-tilt, 10,400 mAh, microSD to 256 GB, IP65. You accept a brand-locked data plan bought in the app and a smaller company behind it.
  • Best camera, and a Wi-Fi fallback: eufy 4G LTE Cam S330. 4K, 9,400 mAh with a 4.5 W panel in the box, a 32 GB card, and a SIM you top up in the eufy app with no contract. $249.99 at eufy.com on 2026-11-06.
  • 4K with your own prepaid data and no Wi-Fi at all: Reolink Go PT Ultra. 21.6 Wh battery rated about two months per charge, prepaid T-Mobile or AT&T data, 2-year warranty. Buy the solar panel bundle if the spot gets sun.
  • Inside your home Wi-Fi but no outlet: Arenti GO1 solar kit ({buy:arenti-go1-outdoor-camera-solar-kit}). Not a cellular camera; it needs 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.

Not recommended

The Arlo Go 2 is a capable LTE-plus-Wi-Fi camera, but it is 1080p, it launched locked to Verizon, and Arlo requires an Arlo Secure subscription on top of the data plan; Arlo's own Trustpilot pages are full of complaints about plan price rises. Skip the no-name 4G cameras that fill marketplace listings at similar prices to the Arenti: their trial lengths, battery sizes and plan prices change from listing to listing, and there is no US phone support when the plan stops working. Arenti at least has a US support line and a 2-year warranty on its site.
